feature_contract.goal: Reduce registry-mutex and hash-lookup overhead in real interleaved D3D9Ex vertex/index-buffer shadow traffic while preserving stereo draw bytes, generation fencing, Reset and final COM release safety.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only R30 per-thread CPU shadow registry lookup and its regression model; no HUD placement, world-eye transforms, F11, main-menu, DX11, DXVK, input, SkyGlow or GPU quality settings.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: Quest3 2026-10-14 recorded up to 3298 draws and 75.6 XR Hz CURRENT_FOCUS with gameRenderCpu p95 11.876 ms/p99 16.179 ms; R30FindShadow proved an explicit two-entry registry-mutex fallback on alternating third/fourth VB/IB addresses. Optimization is a source-based CPU cost hypothesis, not a measured FPS improvement.
trace_stages: Game D3D9 Lock/Unlock stream and CreateBuffer register generation-fenced VB/IB entries with thread-local two-way lookup.
R30 stereo indexed and direct draws resolve CPU shadow pointers before depth classifier, touched-mask decode and per-eye geometry replay.
OpenXR host receives unchanged left/right surfaces; reduced registry lookups cannot change viewport, camera, pose, geometry bytes or GPU shading.
subcomponents: Expand both vertex and index registry lookup caches from two to four independent epoch-fenced slots, without using stale entries across Release/Reset or recycling.
Exercise alternating four-buffer hit behavior, negative pointers and generation transitions in the existing destructive regression and exact-SHA full Win32 host/game gate.

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: In repeated four-buffer VB or IB streams, exactly four initial registry misses occur rather than one lock per interleaved third/fourth buffer; no changes to draw bytes, stereo transforms or shader state.
Generation changes invalidate cached live and absent COM pointers on Reset, Release and re-registration; mutation checks reject dropped fences, broken slot cycling or mixed VB/IB registries.
Original shadow-lookup regression, full DX9Ex Active x86 game/x64 host/package and Domain Isolation succeed at same exact SHA; Quest3 scene-matched frame-time remains separate.

diagnosis.original_evidence: Real Quest3 log shows high game draw count and frame-time tail, while source has two-entry global-mutex fallback for interleaved VB/IB.
diagnosis.root_cause: Two-entry per-thread pointer cache thrashes on three-to-four-buffer working sets, causing repeated registry mutex acquisitions, hash lookups and cache shared_ptr updates. Performance impact not yet measured.
source_trace: R30 observed Lock/Unlock updates buffer registry and epoch under mutex.
R30FindVertexShadow and R30FindIndexShadow resolve pointers on each indexed stereo draw.
The resolved generation-fenced bytes seed or decode unchanged per-eye content before host composition.
alternatives_rejected: Do not blame host-copy time (under 0.01 ms p95 in sample) or conclude 319 ms single-startup spike is dense-scene GPU bound.
Avoid speculative device-loss or full renderer refactor; optimize only verified redundant lookup path.

ci_evidence.expected_workflow: DX9Ex Active Validation + Domain Isolation Guard
ci_evidence.local_model: JS four-address cache miss model=4 for 4096 repeated requests
